tldr: UltraTool is a novel benchmark with 5,824 examples across 22 domains and 2,032 tools that comprehensively evaluates LLMs' tool utilization abilities including planning, creation, and usage in real-world complex scenarios.
contributions: UltraTool is a comprehensive evaluation benchmark derived from complex real-world queries covering six key dimensions in tool utilization
UltraTool explicitly evaluates NL-based planning and advanced tool creation capabilities, eliminating reliance on pre-defined toolsets
Extensive experiments uncover limitations of current LLMs in tool utilization and inspire future research directions
methods: The authors collected real-world user queries from 22+ domains with domain experts, used GPT-4 to generalize and complicate queries, and generated multi-step hierarchical tree-structured plans independently of any predefined toolset. Tools were created as skeletons using GPT-4 when existing tools were insufficient, and all samples underwent manual refinement by six experts. They evaluated closed-source models (GPT-3.5, GPT-4) and open-source models (LLaMA2, ChatGLM3, Baichuan2, Vicuna, Qwen, Mistral) using three metrics: Multi-Dimensional Point-Wise LLM-as-Judge, Key-Value based Accuracy, and Key-Value based Levenshtein Distance across six evaluation dimensions: planning, tool creation awareness, tool creation, tool usage awareness, tool selection, and tool usage.
results: GPT-4 achieved the best overall performance with 76.04% on the Chinese-dataset and 74.58% on the English-dataset. Mistral-7B showed competitive performance relative to its model scale. Larger open-source models performed better, confirming that tool utilization ability improves as model scale increases. Most open-source LLMs demonstrated competitive planning performance but had notable gaps in tool creation and tool usage compared to closed-source models, especially for smaller-scale models.
limitations: The tools in the benchmark are simulated tool skeletons rather than specific implementations. The source data was originally collected in Chinese and required translation to English. The evaluation dimensions for tool creation and tool usage have intricate JSON output format requirements, which pose challenges especially for smaller open-source models.
